name: Popover
summary: Shows anchored contextual content in a dismissible dialog surface.

useWhen: Offering a small interaction tied to its trigger, such as renaming an item
avoidWhen: Running a complex blocking workflow; use Dialog
Describing a control in a short phrase; use Tooltip
Previewing a link or item on hover or focus; use PreviewTrigger

obligations: Expose the trigger relationship, dialog name, and placement.
Contain focus in modal mode and dismiss on Escape or outside focus interaction when enabled.

behavior: A Popover renders in a portal and is positioned against its trigger.
Closing returns focus to the element that was focused when the Popover opened.
If the element that opened the Popover has left the DOM when the Popover closes or unmounts, focus moves to the nearest ancestor recorded at opening that is still connected and focusable.
That move happens only when focus would otherwise be on the document body, and with no such ancestor focus stays there.
When overlays are stacked, Escape closes the topmost one.
trigger is required and must be a focusable React element.
Pressing the trigger toggles the Popover.
Open state is controlled with open and onOpenChange, or starts from defaultOpen when uncontrolled.
placement accepts top, bottom, start, end, top-start, top-end, bottom-start, bottom-end, start-top, start-bottom, end-top, and end-bottom.
start and end resolve through the current locale direction.
An unsupported placement, a non-finite offset or crossOffset, a non-boolean shouldFlip, or a negative or non-finite containerPadding throws a TypeError.
anchorRef positions the Popover against another DOM element, while the trigger still opens it and keeps its accessibility relationships.
With modal set to false, the Popover is non-blocking: it has no focus containment, outside-content exclusion, or scroll locking.
Changing modal while open keeps the existing content, uncontrolled values, and child state.
Entering modal mode focuses the dialog surface when focus is outside it.
Keep the muxui-popover__positioner and muxui-popover selectors, and the data-muxui-state-placement and transition state attributes.
data-muxui-modal on the positioner exposes the modal setting for consumer styling.

colorScheme makes the open Popover a scope of that color scheme: data-muxui-color-scheme is set on the positioner that wraps the surface, so tokens and Mux UI components inside resolve as they do on a page of that scheme, whatever the page uses.

A scoped Popover's surface is that scheme's raised popup surface with the scheme's default text, not the strong surface an unscoped Popover has, because that surface is inverted against its page and Mux UI components inside would not read on it.

A scoped Popover also carries the data-muxui-theme and data-muxui-contrast of the nearest element at or above its trigger that has each, falling back to the document root, because a preset palette is chosen from the attributes on the scope element and the portal sits outside the trigger's surroundings.

The copied attributes are read when the Popover opens and stay live while it is open, so changing either on the trigger, an ancestor, or the document root re-themes the open Popover without reopening it; an attribute that nothing carries is absent from the Popover, and watching stops when it closes.
With colorScheme unset, the Popover adds none of these attributes, renders no extra element, and looks and behaves as before.
A dismissable non-modal Popover also closes on an outside press, and on Escape while focus is on the trigger.
With dismissable set to false, Escape, an outside press, and the trigger do not close the Popover, in modal and non-modal mode.
A button with slot="close" in the content still closes it.
Pressing a close-slot button closes an uncontrolled Popover and calls onOpenChange(false).
A controlled Popover stays open until its owner sets open to false.
accessibility: Expose aria-haspopup and aria-expanded on the trigger.
Require aria-label or aria-labelledby for the dialog content surface.
In non-modal mode, preserve trigger focus on opening and allow focus to leave the content surface.
